summary: This scenario models a single billing cycle where the cardholder makes purchases that stay below the credit limit, receives a statement, and then pays the full statement balance before the due date. It exercises on-time satisfaction of the minimum-payment obligation while preserving the purchase grace-period narrative and avoiding both late and over-limit fees.
assumptions: The prior billing cycle ended with a previous balance of $0.00, so the issuer's grace-period obligation for new purchases is triggered under clause-6-grace-period.
The account credit limit is $1000.00, and total purchases in this cycle never cause the outstanding balance to exceed that limit, satisfying clause-4-credit-limits.
The statement for this cycle closes on 2026-05-31 and sets a payment due date of 2026-06-25, which is at least 25 days later.
The statement new balance is $300.00, so the contractual minimum payment would be max(3% of $300.00, $15.00) = $15.00; the cardholder instead pays the full $300.00.
The payment is made through an approved standard method and is credited on the date received, with no returned payment and no processing delay.
No cash advance, foreign transaction, disputed charge, illegal use, delinquency, or default occurs in this scenario.
Because this archetype is 'on-time full payment,' no fee-triggering conditions occur; accordingly, no late fee or over-limit fee events are included.
